profile.entities: Hindustan Zinc Ltd (Vedanta 60.71%, Govt of India 27.92%). Subs: Hindustan Zinc Alloys Pvt Ltd; Hindmetal Exploration Services Pvt Ltd; a fertilizer subsidiary. Assets: Rampura Agucha (world's largest zinc mine), Sindesar Khurd (6th-largest silver mine globally), Chanderiya Lead-Zinc Smelter, Debari smelter; 6 mines, all in Rajasthan. Partners: Tripura Group + CMR Green Energies (Zinc Park); Serentica (20-yr renewable PPA)
profile.mgmt: Priya Agarwal Hebbar (Chairperson); Arun Misra (CEO & Whole-time Director); Amit Gupta (CFO); Thomas Matthews (ID, Audit & Risk / NRC chair); Dr. Aruna Sharma (Women ID); Anoop Kumar Mittal (ID, SRC chair); Aashhima V. Khanna (Company Secretary & Compliance Officer)
profile.subseg: Zinc; Lead; Silver (primary producer); Zinc-Aluminium-Magnesium & specialty alloys (EcoZen, zinc-nickel for batteries, CGG); by-product cadmium; new: critical minerals (potash, tungsten, rare-earth/neodymium, halite) + fertilizers

assumptions: FY27 refined metal volume of 1.1M tons phased as 260/270/280/290 kt quarterly
Zinc LME averages $2800-2900/t through FY27, below Q4FY26 spot but above FY26 average
Cash cost within $975-1000/t guided range; Q2FY27 benefits from by-product ramp-up
INR 600cr annualised other operating income/expense gross-up removed from projections (normalised P&L)
Hedging drag of ~INR 300-400cr per quarter continues, embedded in OPM
Effective tax rate ~25%, consistent with recent quarters
INR/USD assumed ~83, consistent with recent realised rates

projection.rationale: Revenue declines sequentially from Q4FY26 peak due to lower zinc prices and normalised volumes (~260kt refined), but remains well above Q1FY26. OPM at 53% reflects cost guidance of $975-1000/ton and removal of Q4's INR 600cr gross-up, partially offset by hedging drag.

Modest sequential volume improvement to ~270kt and steady LME. OPM ticks up to 54% as fertiliser plant and hot acid leaching ramp up, boosting by-product credits and lowering net cost toward $975/ton. PAT reflects stable other income and tax rate.

Volume reaches ~280kt as Debari smelter contributes initial tonnes. OPM expands to 55% on higher grade (7.3-7.4%) and RE share reaching 30%, reducing power cost. Revenue growth muted YoY as Q3FY26 had an exceptionally high 55.1% OPM base.

Full-year exit rate of ~290kt refined metal; revenue capped by normalised zinc prices (~$2900). OPM sustained at 55% as cost stays within guided band. PAT growth QoQ from operating leverage, but YoY decline due to absence of Q4FY26's INR 600cr gross-up and favourable one-offs.

bull_bear.body:
- **Self-funded growth + maintained returns:** capex covered by accruals; dividends preserved. Dividend ₹11/sh FY26 (vs ₹10). Balance sheet "very strong," ~67% ROCE / ~77% ROE.
- **Ownership:** Vedanta 60.71%, Govt of India 27.92%. GoI continues to trim ~2–3%/yr (disinvestment) — management frames this as improving float/price discovery, "nothing for us to do."
- Shareholder asks (bonus/higher dividend for the 60th-year "Diamond Jubilee") noted; no bonus announced.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Silver price crash:** silver reportedly fell from ~₹4.24 lakh/kg to ~₹2.44 lakh/kg → the recent share-price "shakedown"; with silver ~50% of profit, earnings are highly silver-price-geared. Management says metals (incl. silver) stay "directionally strong" over 4–5 years.
- **Zinc price competition from China** — flagged by shareholders; countered by low-cost position + domestic demand.
- **Govt disinvestment overhang** (2–3%/yr) on share price.
- **Geopolitics / Middle-East / war:** mitigated by pre-emptively **shifting the sales market from Middle-East to Southeast Asia** before the crisis escalated — "profit not impacted."
- **Aravalli Supreme Court verdict:** **no impact** — existing operating mines continue as-is per the court's own carve-out for existing operations.
- **Concentration:** all mines in Rajasthan; commodity/earnings volatility inherent.
- **Execution/slippage:** the ₹40–50,000cr, 5-year, multi-smelter build is the key execution watch (Phase-1 Debari smelter timeline).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Confident, strategy-led; strong governance signalling (No.1 in S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment for metals/mining 3 years running; only Indian ICMM member; top-1% S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook 2026; Zinc Mark certification at Chanderiya & Rampura Agucha). Founder-family leadership (Priya Agarwal Hebbar, daughter of Anil Agarwal). CEO Arun Misra answered nearly all shareholder queries directly and specifically (capex funding, COP, critical minerals, power).
- Note: several retail shareholders referred to a "CFO Sandeep Modi" / "Navin Agarwal Executive Director," but the official board introduction named **Amit Gupta as CFO** and Priya Agarwal Hebbar as Chairperson — used here.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **HZL is now a silver story as much as a zinc story** — ~50% of profit is silver, 100% sold in India (insulated from export tariffs, fully exposed to domestic silver price). The 700 t → 1,500 t silver ramp is the biggest single earnings lever.
- **"Zung ke khilaaf Zinc"** is a genuine demand-creation moat play: getting India-sold cars galvanized (currently they aren't; exports are) structurally lifts domestic zinc demand.
- **Critical-minerals optionality is real, not slideware:** actual auction wins in tungsten, potash, RE (neodymium), halite — with fertilizer/potash and magnet/neodymium synergies mapped to national import-substitution priorities (India meets only ~10% of critical-mineral demand domestically even by 2031).
- **Self-funding the 2X is the underappreciated point:** ₹60–65,000cr of 5-yr PAT vs ₹40–45,000cr capex means no equity dilution and preserved dividends — rare for a doubling of capacity.
- **Subsidiary value-unlock** (listing/demerger of Hindustan Zinc Alloys / Hindmetal Exploration) floated by shareholders as future optionality; management non-committal.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Clear dividend policy: minimum 30% of PAT or 5% of opening net worth, whichever is higher; delivered ~5.6% dividend yield.
- Focus on maximizing total shareholder returns; FY25 TSR of ~68% (₹198.60 per share), 13x NIFTY 50 returns.
- Maintains AAA credit rating and industry-leading balance sheet; FY25 ROCE of 58% and ROE of 73%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- **Funding math disclosed explicitly:** run-rate PAT of ₹12,000–13,000 crore/year → ~₹60,000–65,000
  crore over 5 years, against a ~₹40,000–45,000 crore capex need. Management's framing: **capex is
  fully funded from internal accruals "without hurting any shareholder gains,"** with debt used only
  opportunistically to match cash-flow timing — reads as an implicit **no-dilution signal** (no rights
  issue/QIP flagged) even though a shareholder directly asked whether a rights issue or QIP would be
  used.
- **Dividend track record cited:** FY26 final dividend ₹10/share; **first FY27 interim dividend already
  declared at ₹11/share** (paid Apr/May 2026) — consistent with the "minimum 30% payout" policy noted
  in the Q4FY26 concall note.
- **Total shareholder return since the 2002 disinvestment:** ~₹787/share including ~₹285.55/share of
  cumulative dividends — cited by management as …
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation & dividend signals (AGM 2026)

bull_bear.body:
- Chairperson's speech was aspirational and identity-shifting ("the best chapters of Hindustan Zinc
  are not behind us"), leaning into the metals-to-energy-transition repositioning and citing
  India's projected 2031 critical-minerals demand-supply gap (domestic production meeting only ~10%
  of national demand) as the strategic opportunity.
  CEO Arun Misra's tone was confident/comprehensive — his single consolidated Q&A response covered
  nearly every shareholder question in one pass (a shareholder jokingly noted this left nothing
  for others to ask).
- **Clean audit opinion** — no qualification, modified opinion, or adverse remarks; notice/auditor's
  report were taken as read given no exceptions.
- **Governance recognition:** first Indian company in ICMM; #1 global ranking in metals & mining on
  S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment for the 3rd consecutive year; top 1% …
bull_bear.title: Management tone & governance (AGM 2026)

business.body:
- **Zinc / Lead:** core integrated miner-smelter; world's largest integrated zinc producer; Rampura Agucha now world's largest zinc mine.
- **Silver:** Sindesar Khurd = 6th-largest silver mine globally; ~50% of profit; demand driven by solar/renewables, electronics, advanced tech; US and others declaring silver a critical mineral.
- **Alloys / value-add:** zinc-aluminium-magnesium alloy (for steel industry — aims to be pioneer/market leader), EcoZen, zinc-nickel for batteries, special CGG products.
- **Subsidiaries:** Hindustan Zinc Alloys Pvt Ltd; Hindmetal Exploration Services Pvt Ltd (exploration + critical-mineral pipeline); a fertilizer subsidiary (synergy with potash). A shareholder pressed for **listing / demerger of subsidiaries** to unlock value; management did not commit.

latest_quarter.body:
- **Power is 40–45% of production cost** — the single biggest cost lever.
- **Serentica 20-year renewable PPA:** blended renewable cost is **lower** than HZL's own thermal + grid purchase → simultaneously cuts cost *and* CO2 (supports the 70%-RE-by-FY28 and net-zero-by-2060 goals).
- Powerhouses modified to burn **domestic coal** (cost); RTC renewable via central-grid tie-in — **wind from Maharashtra, solar from Rajasthan, plus battery backup in Rajasthan** for round-the-clock RE.
- Cost leadership framed as cycle-resilience, not just margin: keeps HZL profitable through commodity volatility.

latest_quarter.body:

Silver target 700→1,500t at 2Mt. Critical-minerals entry (tungsten/potash/RE-neodymium/halite blocks won). 70% RE by FY28 via Serentica 20-yr PPA. FY27 production guide ~1.1 Mt.

outlook.body:
- **Production (FY27):** ~1.1 Mt metal (guidance given to market).
- **"2X" volume:** double metal production from 1.1 Mt → **2 Mt over the next 5 years** (phased, brownfield + de-bottlenecking).
- **Silver:** at 2 Mt scale, produce **>1,500 t of silver** (from ~700 t currently); India consumes ~7,000–8,000 t, HZL is ~10% of that.
- **Capex:** total program **₹40,000–50,000 cr** (Misra narrowed to ₹40,000–45,000cr). **Phase-1 ₹17,000cr already Board-approved** in FY26.
- **Cost:** maintain COP ~$950/t **despite** expansion (higher mining intensity) — lever is renewable power (see §7).
- **Renewables:** **70% renewable energy by FY2028**.
- **Reserves & mine life:** grow metal R&R to **50 Mt**; maintain mine life **>25 years** alongside expansion.
- **Portfolio:** add **~3 new metals** in next 5 years (from neodymium / potash / tungsten / possibly gold or copper blocks).
- **Cash generation:** PAT to stay **₹12,000–13,000cr/yr** at current level → **~₹60–65,000cr over 5 years**, enough to fully fund the ₹40–45,000cr capex from internal accrual without hurting dividends.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: - Not an order-book business (commodity producer). Demand anchors flagged: India steel output **150 Mt → 300 Mt** planned → more infra/galvanization → structural zinc pull; ~70–75% domestic zinc market share; silver sold **100% domestically** (not an ounce exported).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Critical minerals (the pivot):** secured government-auction blocks in **tungsten, potash, rare-earth (monazite → neodymium, UP), and halite**. HZL would be India's **first potash miner** (India imports all potash today — perfect synergy with its fertilizer arm) and **first tungsten miner**. The UP monazite block can yield **neodymium** — the key metal for magnets (EV/electromagnets); HZL intends to bid in the government's magnet-manufacturing auction. Aggressively participating in all Critical Mineral Mission auctions.
- **Zinc Park:** with **Tripura Group + CMR Green Energies** — "India's first integrated zinc manufacturing ecosystem," pulling MSMEs into the value chain.
- **Tailings reprocessing:** India's first zinc-tailings reprocessing plant (part of Phase-1) — legacy waste → resource.
- **Digital / "technology-led" pivot:** vision to move from "a metals company using technology" to "a technology-led company that also produces metals" (HZL 2.0); AI-enabled/automated/intelligent mining, advanced analytics; Zincky Sonic (Gen-AI annual-report chatbot).
- **Galvanization demand-creation ("Zung ke khilaaf Zinc"):** campaign educating auto OEMs that India-sold cars are *not* galvanized while exported cars *are* — pushing domestic galvanization = a structural zinc-demand lever.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
Chairperson Priya Agarwal Hebbar reframed the company's ambition from "world's leading integrated
zinc producer" to a **"future-ready energy transition company"** — building strength across multiple
metals rather than remaining zinc-only. The core commitments:
- **2X volume plan:** double total metal production from **1.1 million tonnes to 2 million tonnes over
  the next 5 years**, via brownfield expansion + de-bottlenecking (no new-geography greenfield
  mentioned).
- **Capex envelope:** **₹40,000–50,000 crore** multi-year programme (CEO later reiterated as "40 to
  45,000 crore" in the Q&A). **Phase 1 of ₹17,000 crore already Board-approved in FY26**, covering a
  **250,000 TPA integrated zinc smelter at Debari** and **India's first zinc tailings-reprocessing
  plant**. Balance ₹23,000–33,000 crore of the programme is not yet phase-approved — watch for
  slippage/approval cadence.
- …
outlook.title: Strategic vision (the 5-year story) (AGM 2026)

deepdive.thesis: HZL delivered a record FY26 — first-ever ₹40,000cr+ revenue and ₹20,000cr+ EBITDA (~54% margin), ₹13,832cr PAT (EPS ~₹33), an 18-year-high ~67% ROCE / ~77% ROE, and a 5-year-low zinc cost of production of $959/t (ex-royalty). The forward story is the **"2X" plan**: double metal output from 1.1 Mt to 2 Mt over the next 5 years via a ₹40,000–50,000cr capex program (Phase-1 ₹17,000cr already approved) — comfortably self-funded from ~₹60–65,000cr of cumulative PAT, so shareholder returns need not be sacrificed. Silver (~50% of profit, sold 100% domestically) is now the earnings swing factor and its recent price crash is the near-term overhang; the longer optionality is a deliberate pivot into critical minerals (potash, tungsten, rare-earth/neodymium magnets) positioning HZL as a "future-ready energy-transition company."
